purpose: Evidence registry for movement-quality assessment and research-only injury-association features. Entries do not automatically become runtime thresholds.

evidence.measurementMethod: Kinect and Vicon rehabilitation movement dataset
evidence.signal: Non-optimal deep squat protocol includes inability to squat past parallel, knee valgus collapse, loss of upright trunk posture, and trunk flexion greater than 30 degrees.
evidence.limitations: Protocol-defined non-optimal form is not equivalent to prospective injury risk. Vicon/Kinect measures are not automatically interchangeable with MediaPipe 2D webcam angles.

evidence.measurementMethod: RGB-D Kinect skeleton plus physician-defined features and clinician performance scores
evidence.population: 44 healthy subjects and 34 subjects with motor dysfunctions
evidence.signal: Clinician-scored exercise quality for five rehabilitation exercises.
evidence.limitations: Clinical score is exercise-quality ground truth, not future-injury ground truth; sensor/domain shift to a monocular webcam must be validated.

evidence.measurementMethod: Azure Kinect RGB-D and skeleton joints
evidence.signal: Paired correct and incorrect forms of the same exercises and subjects.
evidence.limitations: Small cohort and RGB-D sensor; useful for form classification but not prospective injury prediction.

evidence.sourceLabel: Raisanen et al. prospective frontal-plane knee control study
evidence.measurementMethod: 2D frontal-plane knee projection angle during single-leg squat using anatomical landmarks
evidence.population: 306 young basketball and floorball athletes with 12-month follow-up
evidence.signal: FPKPA greater than 23.8 degrees was associated with subsequent acute lower-extremity injury (adjusted OR 2.67, 95% CI 1.23-5.83).
evidence.limitations: AUC was poor for screening; study metric uses ASIS-knee-ankle geometry, while BlazePose does not provide true ASIS landmarks. Do not map 23.8 degrees directly to the current MediaPipe proxy.

evidence.sourceLabel: Nakagawa et al. prospective patellofemoral pain study
evidence.measurementMethod: Single-leg squat frontal-plane knee projection angle
evidence.signal: FPKPA >= 4.81 degrees was associated with development of patellofemoral pain in the study cohort.
evidence.limitations: Population-specific; not a general injury threshold and not directly transferable to BlazePose geometry without validation.

evidence.sourceLabel: Hewett et al. prospective ACL biomechanics study
evidence.measurementMethod: 3D kinematics and kinetics during jump landing
evidence.population: 205 female high-school athletes; 9 subsequent ACL ruptures
evidence.signal: Subsequently injured athletes showed greater knee abduction and loading during landing.
evidence.limitations: 3D lab kinematics/kinetics and force data cannot be converted into a monocular 2D webcam threshold.

evidence.sourceLabel: Paterno et al. prospective second ACL injury study
evidence.measurementMethod: 3D motion analysis during drop vertical jump plus postural stability testing
evidence.population: 56 athletes after ACL reconstruction followed for 12 months; 13 sustained a second ACL injury
evidence.signal: A multifactorial model incorporating hip/knee mechanics and postural stability discriminated second ACL injury in the study cohort (C statistic 0.94; sensitivity 0.92; specificity 0.88).
evidence.limitations: Small post-ACLR population, 3D kinetics and Biodex stability measurements are unavailable from the current webcam. The reported performance must not be transferred to this system.

evidence.sourceLabel: Krosshaug et al. prospective cohort of elite female soccer and handball players
evidence.population: 710 analyzed athletes; 42 new noncontact ACL injuries
evidence.signal: Selected landing variables had poor screening discrimination; among athletes without prior injury, none of the tested variables were associated with increased ACL injury risk.
evidence.limitations: Supports blocking simplistic landing-angle injury prediction even when sophisticated laboratory measures are available.

evidence.sourceLabel: Nilstad et al. elite female athlete 2D screening study
evidence.measurementMethod: 2D video measures of frontal-plane knee and hip control
evidence.population: 778 eligible elite female football/handball athletes; 56 future noncontact ACL injuries
evidence.signal: Frontal-plane knee projection angle, medial knee position, lateral pelvic tilt and asymmetry did not discriminate future ACL injury.
evidence.limitations: Directly cautions against converting common 2D webcam frontal-plane measures into a future ACL injury prediction.

evidence.sourceLabel: Multidisciplinary prediction of running-related injuries using machine learning
evidence.measurementMethod: Weekly prospective machine-learning dataset combining genetics, history, strength, biomechanics, body composition, nutrition, and training
evidence.population: 142 competitive endurance runners monitored for 12 months; 6,181 weekly samples
evidence.signal: Multifactorial models achieved approximately 0.784 mean AUC for weekly running-related injury prediction.
evidence.limitations: Demonstrates that useful prognostic modeling is multifactorial and still imperfect. It must not be reduced to webcam pose alone or used to claim universal injury prediction.

evidence.sourceLabel: Systematic review and meta-analysis of knee abduction and future ACL injury
evidence.measurementMethod: Prospective studies of 2D/3D knee abduction kinematics and kinetics
evidence.signal: Meta-analysis did not find knee abduction measures alone to consistently predict future ACL injury.
evidence.limitations: Supports avoiding a single-metric ACL prediction claim.

evidence.sourceLabel: Avci et al. squat task injury-risk systematic review
evidence.measurementMethod: Systematic review of squat-based injury-risk assessment
evidence.signal: Squat assessment may contribute information, but included methods were heterogeneous and some studies concluded squat alone is insufficient.
evidence.limitations: Does not justify black-and-white injury prediction from squat form alone.
